NNS ANOVA: Nonparametric Analysis of Variance

Source: R/ANOVA.R
NNS.ANOVA.Rd

Compares control and treatment groups through benchmark-relative partial moments. The chosen mode compares means, medians, or a distribution profile with central and tail benchmarks, without selecting a parametric family.

Usage

NNS.ANOVA(
  control,
  treatment,
  means.only = FALSE,
  medians = FALSE,
  confidence.interval = 0.95,
  tails = "Both",
  pairwise = FALSE,
  plot = TRUE,
  robust = FALSE
)

Arguments

control

Numeric vector of control group observations

treatment

Numeric vector of treatment group observations

means.only

Logical; FALSE (default) uses full distribution analysis. Set TRUE for the central comparison only (means, or medians when medians = TRUE)

medians

Logical; FALSE (default) uses means. Set TRUE for median-based analysis

confidence.interval

Numeric [0,1]; confidence level for effect size bounds (e.g., 0.95)

tails

Character; specifies CI tail(s): "both", "left", or "right"

pairwise

logical; FALSE (default) Returns pairwise certainty tests when set to pairwise = TRUE.

plot

Logical; TRUE (default) generates distribution plot

robust

logical; FALSE (default) Two-sample (control, treatment) path only: draws 100 independent bootstrap resamples of each group (with replacement, from its own full sample), and returns / plots the robust central tendency (NNS.gravity) and the confidence.interval bounds of the resampled Certainty values. It is ignored when control is a matrix or list (multi-group, including pairwise = TRUE).

Value

Returns a list containing:

  • Control: Mean/median of control group

  • Treatment: Mean/median of treatment group

  • Grand_Statistic: Mean/median of all observations pooled

  • Control_CDF: CDF value at grand statistic (control)

  • Treatment_CDF: CDF value at grand statistic (treatment)

  • Certainty: Agreement index for the chosen central or distribution-profile comparison, with the finite-sample adjustment; not a calibrated probability.

  • Effect_Size_LB: Lower bound of treatment effect (if confidence.interval requested)

  • Effect_Size_UB: Upper bound of treatment effect (if confidence.interval requested)

  • Confidence_Level: Confidence level used (if confidence.interval requested)

Details

The key output, Certainty, is a descriptive agreement index in \([0, 1]\) for the chosen target:

  • means.only = TRUE, medians = FALSE: compares group means using degree-one deviation-area ratios at the pooled mean.

  • means.only = TRUE, medians = TRUE: compares medians using the distance of 0.5 from each interval \([F(t-), F(t)]\) at the pooled median \(t\). This interval contains 0.5 exactly when \(t\) is a median, including tied and discrete data.

  • means.only = FALSE: adds the 12.5% and 25% lower and upper deviation-area benchmarks to the chosen central comparison. This examines distributional shape through a finite profile; agreement at these benchmarks does not prove equality of laws.

At a constant group's only value both deviation areas vanish. For agreement comparisons this satisfies the expectile balance at every level, so its area discrepancy is zero there. Returned CDF values retain the public partial-moment step convention; other benchmarks and nonconstant samples use the ordinary ratio discrepancy.

The raw score is 1 at maximal benchmark agreement. The returned score is multiplied by \(((n_1 + n_2 - 2)/(n_1 + n_2))^2\), so the finite-sample maximum is below 1. Certainty is not a calibrated probability, a p-value, or statistical power, and has no universal significance cutoff. Equal population means need not produce the same score distribution when sample sizes or spreads differ. robust = TRUE describes sampling variability of the score; it does not generate a null reference distribution.

Random relabelings of the pooled observations provide a reference under identical distributions only when observations are exchangeable. They are not a general unequal-variance equal-means test. Any inferential calibration must match the chosen target and the sampling design; dependent observations require a suitable resampling design.

Effect-size bounds retain the conservative difference of the groups' separate bootstrap endpoints. They are not quantiles of the bootstrap difference and need not have exactly the requested nominal coverage. The independent-group bootstrap assumes independent observations within and between groups.

References

Viole, F. and Nawrocki, D. (2013) "Nonlinear Nonparametric Statistics: Using Partial Moments" (ISBN: 1490523995, 2nd edition: https://ovvo-financial.github.io/NNS/book/)

Viole, F. (2017) "Continuous CDFs and ANOVA with NNS" doi:10.2139/ssrn.3007373

Author

Fred Viole, OVVO Financial Systems

Examples

 if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
### Binary analysis and effect size
set.seed(123)
x <- rnorm(100) ; y <- rnorm(100)
NNS.ANOVA(control = x, treatment = y)

### Two variable analysis with no control variable
A <- cbind(x, y)
NNS.ANOVA(A)

### Medians test
NNS.ANOVA(A, means.only = TRUE, medians = TRUE)

### Multiple variable analysis with no control variable
set.seed(123)
x <- rnorm(100) ; y <- rnorm(100) ; z <- rnorm(100)
A <- cbind(x, y, z)
NNS.ANOVA(A)

### Different length vectors used in a list
x <- rnorm(30) ; y <- rnorm(40) ; z <- rnorm(50)
A <- list(x, y, z)
NNS.ANOVA(A)
} # }
